title: Typing | Loanwords
description: This course is designed for the continued practice of typing skills after the basics of touch typing have been mastered. The lessons delve into loanwords that have come into English from around the globe, combining definitions, etymology, and the words in context in over 400 typing lessons and games.

lessons.name: Intro 1
lessons.text1:
Get ready to type all about loanwords!
Loanwords are words borrowed from other languages with little or no changes.

instruction.body: Before starting this course, you should complete a RETROSPEED course that covers the basics! We'll be using a variety of letters, numbers, and symbols on the keyboard.

lessons.name: Intro 2
lessons.text1: We'll type examples of loanwords from around the globe that have helped make English the rich language that it is today.

lessons.name: Intro 3
lessons.text1: We'll type the definition and etymology (the history of the word) of each loanword, as well as sentences and paragraphs that use the words.

lessons.name: Intro 4
lessons.text1: Some loanwords might be new to you, while you might use others every day without realizing that they came from other languages!

lessons.name: Intro 5
lessons.text1: Are you ready to type and learn more about loanwords? Let's go!

lessons.name: Spanish Intro
lessons.text1: Spanish is the official language of 20 sovereign states, including Spain and many countries in Central and South America. There are about 500 million native Spanish speakers worldwide.

lessons.name: Cafeteria: Definition
lessons.text1: cafeteria (noun): a restaurant in which the customers serve themselves or are served at a counter and take the food to tables to eat.

lessons.name: Cafeteria: History
lessons.text1: "Cafeteria" comes from 19th century Latin American Spanish. The first half of the word means "coffee," so the word originally referred to a coffee shop.

lessons.name: Cafeteria: Sentence
lessons.text1: We went down to the school cafeteria at lunch time. I chose the pizza and my friend got the pasta.

lessons.name: Bronco: Definition
lessons.text1: bronco (noun): a wild or half-tamed horse of the western United States.

lessons.name: Bronco: History
lessons.text1: "Bronco" comes from mid-19th century Latin American Spanish. Literally translated, it means "rude" or "rough."

lessons.name: Bronco: Sentence
lessons.text1: We saw a lot of animals at the ranch, including sheep, sheepdogs, and a new bronco.

lessons.name: Patio: Definition
lessons.text1: patio (noun): an area outside a house with a solid floor but no roof, used in good weather for relaxing, eating, etc.

lessons.name: Patio: History
lessons.text1: Starting in the mid-18th century, "patio" was used in Spanish to mean "courtyard." In modern English it may still mean a courtyard, but it can also refer to an area next to a building and not necessarily enclosed.

lessons.name: Patio: Sentence
lessons.text1: When the weather is nice in the evening, we like to have dinner out on the patio.

lessons.name: Burrito: Definition
lessons.text1: burrito (noun): a common cylindrical food item of Mexican and American origin consisting of a tortilla wrapped around a mixed filling of such ingredients as meat, cheese, beans, and vegetables.

lessons.name: Burrito: History
lessons.text1: Literally translated, "burrito" means "little donkey," but the story of how the burrito got its name is a mystery. Some say it's because the shape of a burrito is similar to the bedrolls that Mexican miners and travelers used to carry on their donkeys. Others say it's because people who made and sold burritos would carry them on their donkeys.

lessons.name: Burrito: Sentence
lessons.text1: Burritos are my favorite food. They can be filled with anything!

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: patio courtyard outside Spanish house burrito filling wrapped donkey tortilla

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: David went down to the cafeteria for lunch. It was burrito day! He put a burrito and a drink on his tray and looked around for a seat with his friend Andre. But Andre wasn't in the cafeteria. He stayed back at his family's farm to see the new bronco his uncle had just brought in. He could see the pasture from the patio next to the house. He sent David a picture!

lessons.name: Cantonese Intro
lessons.text1: Cantonese is one of many Chinese languages. It originated in Guangzhou in southern China and is spoken in the neighboring areas of Guangdong and Guangxi, as well as in Hong Kong and Macau. It has about 82 million native speakers worldwide.

lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some English words that were originally from Cantonese.

lessons.name: Wonton: Definition
lessons.text1: wonton (noun): a small dumpling typically filled with meat, seafood, or vegetables and usually served boiled in soup or fried.

lessons.name: Wonton: History
lessons.text1: "Wonton" literally translates to "filled dumpling" in Cantonese. The wrapper is typically square and sealed with an egg wash that keeps the filling ingredients inside.

lessons.name: Wonton: Sentence
lessons.text1: The best wonton I ever ate had a thin, chewy wrapper and a filling of meat with fresh herbs.

lessons.name: Kumquat: Definition
lessons.text1: kumquat (noun): a small yellow or orange citrus fruit with a sweet, spongy rind and somewhat acid pulp that is used often for preserves.

lessons.name: Kumquat: History
lessons.text1: "Kumquat" means "golden orange" in Cantonese. The word has been recorded in English since the 1690s.

lessons.name: Kumquat: Sentence
lessons.text1: The kumquat was sweet and sour with a slightly bitter taste from the peel.

lessons.name: Kung fu: Definition
lessons.text1: kung fu (noun): a general term for Chinese martial arts and related disciplines that are practiced especially for self-defense, exercise, and spiritual growth.

lessons.name: Kung fu: History
lessons.text1: The word "kung fu" comes from a Cantonese term meaning "skill achieved through great effort." It only became widely known in English in the 1960s when Bruce Lee became a popular martial artist.

lessons.name: Kung fu: Sentence
lessons.text1: The movie is about a great kung fu fighter who must travel through the mountains and take revenge on his enemies.

lessons.name: Wok: Definition
lessons.text1: wok (noun): a large bowl-shaped cooking pan used especially in stir-frying.

lessons.name: Wok: History
lessons.text1: The word "wok" comes from Cantonese and has migrated not only into English, but many other languages such as Czech, Swedish, Dutch, and Portuguese.

lessons.name: Algonquian Languages Intro
lessons.text1: The Algonquian languages are a large family of languages spoken by First Nation tribes in North America. These languages include M'ikmaq, Ojibwe, Powhatan, and many others. The English language has adopted many Algonquian words, especially words related to nature and wildlife.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that came to English from the Algonquian language family.

lessons.name: Caribou: Definition
lessons.text1: caribou (noun): a species of large deer living in northern regions, also known as reindeer.

lessons.name: Caribou: History
lessons.text1: The word "caribou" comes from the Mi'kmaq word "qalipu," which means "snow shoveler." This name refers to the way caribou paw through snow with their front feet in order to feed on the vegetation underneath.

lessons.name: Caribou: Sentence
lessons.text1: Caribou antlers bobbed over the surface of the water as the herd swam across the river.

lessons.name: Chipmunk: Definition
lessons.text1: chipmunk (noun): a small burrowing rodent with cheek pouches and a striped back.

lessons.name: Chipmunk: History
lessons.text1: "Chipmunk" is thought to be derived from the Ojibwe word "ajidamoo," meaning "one who descends trees headfirst." While the Ojibwe word actually refers to red squirrels, the English word refers to smaller, striped creatures that spend most of their time on the ground.

lessons.name: Chipmunk: Sentence
lessons.text1: The chipmunk poked its nose from its burrow to sniff the air before scurrying across the forest floor in search of acorns.

lessons.name: Moccasin: Definition
lessons.text1: moccasin (noun): a soft, heelless leather shoe traditionally worn by certain Native American tribes.

lessons.name: Moccasin: History
lessons.text1: "Moccasin" comes from the Powhatan word "makasin," meaning "shoe." Traditionally, each shoe was made up of a single piece of deerskin drawn up around the foot and sewn together at the front and the heel.

lessons.name: Moccasin: Sentence
lessons.text1: Her moccasins were soft and covered in intricate, colorful beading.

lessons.name: Raccoon: Definition
lessons.text1: raccoon (noun): a small nocturnal animal with gray fur, a black mask, and a bushy ringed tail.

lessons.name: Raccoon: History
lessons.text1: "Raccoon" is derived from the Powhatan word "arakun," meaning "he who scratches with his hands." This refers to the raccoon's skillful front paws, which it uses to grasp and manipulate food and other objects.

lessons.name: Raccoon: Sentence
lessons.text1: The lid of the trash can was no match for the raccoon's determination and nimble paws.

lessons.text1: On our trip to the National Museum of the American Indian, we saw lots of fascinating cultural objects, including a pair of beaded moccasins and a spear made from caribou antlers. I bought a wooden raccoon figurine in the gift shop. Later, we went on a nature walk, where I saw chipmunks scurrying across the path.

lessons.name: French Intro
lessons.text1: French is an official language in 27 countries and is spoken on every continent, making it one of the most widespread languages. There are approximately 76 million native French speakers, 235 million fluent French speakers, and 321 million total French speakers around the world.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that came to English from French.

lessons.name: Chef: Definition
lessons.text1: chef (noun): a skilled professional cook.

lessons.name: Chef: History
lessons.text1: The word "chef" comes from the French word for "head" or "leader." It originates from the French term "chef de cuisine," meaning "the head of the kitchen."

lessons.name: Chef: Sentence
lessons.text1: The chef cooked a delicious meal for everyone, featuring a perfectly roasted chicken with garlic mashed potatoes and a side of steamed vegetables.

lessons.name: Chic: Definition
lessons.text1: chic (adjective): elegantly fashionable.

lessons.name: Chic: History
lessons.text1: "Chic" comes from the French word meaning "stylish" or "elegant." It was adopted into English in the 19th century to describe someone or something that is fashionable and sophisticated.

lessons.name: Chic: Sentence
lessons.text1: She looked very chic at the party in a stylish silk dress, red high-heeled shoes, and a fancy beret.

lessons.name: Genre: Definition
lessons.text1: genre (noun): a category of artistic, musical, or literary composition characterized by a particular style, form, or content.

lessons.name: Genre: History
lessons.text1: The word "genre" comes from the French word for "kind" or "type." In English, it is mainly used to classify different categories of art, literature, and music.

lessons.name: Genre: Sentence
lessons.text1: His favorite genre of literature is historical fiction because it blends rich narratives with real historical events.

lessons.name: Sabotage: Definition
lessons.text1: sabotage (verb): to deliberately destroy, damage, or obstruct something, especially for political or military advantage.

lessons.name: Sabotage: History
lessons.text1: "Sabotage" comes from the French word "saboter," which means to "bungle" or "wreck," and also the word "sabot," meaning a heavy wooden work shoe. It originally referred to labor disputes where workers would disrupt production as a form of protest.

lessons.name: Sabotage: Sentence
lessons.text1: At recess, my best friend tried to sabotage the football game by hiding the ball.

The heroine, dressed in a chic gown and sparkling shoes, uncovers a plot to sabotage the event. With quick thinking and bravery, she foils the mischievous plan and saves the day!

lessons.name: Arabic Intro
lessons.text1: Arabic is spoken in 22 countries across North Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Middle East. The language has approximately 200 million native speakers and is the original language of the Quran, the Holy Book of Islam.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Several words began in Arabic, were adopted into other languages like French, and then became part of English. Let's practice typing a few of them.

lessons.name: Cotton: Definition
lessons.text1: cotton (noun): a plant grown in warm climates that produces the soft, fluffy fibers used to make the fabric also known as cotton.

lessons.name: Cotton: History
lessons.text1: "Cotton" began as the Arabic word transcribed as "qutn" which may have originated in Egypt. It was adopted into French in the 12th century as "coton" before making its way into English in the 13th century.

lessons.name: Cotton: Sentence
lessons.text1: The cotton fields didn't produce as much as usual last year due to the drought.

lessons.name: Sofa: Definition
lessons.text1: sofa (noun): a long upholstered seat for more than two people, usually with arms and a back.

lessons.name: Sofa: History
lessons.text1: The word "sofa" existed in French, Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese before it came to English. It made its way into those romance languages from the Arabic "soffah".

lessons.name: Sofa: Sentence
lessons.text1: At the end of a long day, they all stretched out on the sofa to relax.

lessons.name: Magazine: Definition
lessons.text1: magazine (noun): a publication issued periodically that typically contains essays, stories, photographs, drawings, etc., by many writers, frequently specializing in a particular subject.

lessons.name: Magazine: History
lessons.text1: The Arabic "makhazin," meaning "storehouses," turned into the Italian "magazzino," or "depot." This turned into the French "magasin," meaning "store," and then became the English "magazine," referring figuratively to a storehouse of information.

lessons.name: Magazine: Sentence
lessons.text1: The newsstand had magazines on every topic from celebrity gossip to fly fishing.

lessons.name: Safari: Definition
lessons.text1: safari (noun): a journey or expedition for hunting, exploration, or investigation, especially in eastern Africa.

lessons.name: Safari: History
lessons.text1: The Arabic "safar" means "journey." This turned into "safari" in the East African language of Kiswahili, where it held the same meaning as it does in English today.

lessons.name: Safari: Sentence
lessons.text1: They were lucky enough to see elephants and giraffes on their safari last year.

It described the societies of elephants in East Africa, and I knew I had to go on safari to see them myself. I booked a ticket, packed my lightest cotton clothing in a suitcase, and went straight to the airport!

lessons.name: Arawakan Languages Intro
lessons.text1: The Arawakan language group comprises several related languages spoken by people native to the northern part of South America, the eastern part of Central America, and parts of the Caribbean.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practicing typing a few words that come from the Arawakan language family.

lessons.name: Barbecue: Definition
lessons.text1: barbecue (noun): a piece of equipment used for cooking food in the open air. Also, a social event where food is prepared in this way.

lessons.name: Barbecue: History
lessons.text1: "Barbecue" was originally "barbakoa." This Arawakan word from present-day Haiti meant "wooden frame on posts," referring to structures used for sleeping or for curing meat. This word was adopted into Spanish as "barbacoa" before coming into English as "barbecue."

lessons.name: Barbecue: Sentence
lessons.text1: She went outside to clean and preheat the barbecue. They were going to grill corn, chicken, and peppers.

lessons.name: Savanna: Definition
lessons.text1: savanna (noun): a flat grassland with sparse trees, usually in subtropical or tropical climates.

lessons.name: Savanna: History
lessons.text1: The Arawakan word "zabana" meant "a low marshy piece of land." It moved into Spanish as "sabana," which means both "sheet" and "treeless plain." English took the word as "savannah" or "savanna," keeping the "treeless plain" definition.

lessons.name: Savanna: Sentence
lessons.text1: Savannas can be found in many places around the world, such as Florida, Eastern Africa, Australia, or Brazil.

lessons.name: Hammock: Definition
lessons.text1: hammock (noun): a strong piece of fabric or netting hung off the ground between two supports and used to lie down in.

lessons.name: Hammock: History
lessons.text1: The Haitian Arawakan word "amaca" meant "fishnet" when the Spanish first arrived in the Caribbean. It was brought into Spanish as "hamaca" and then into English as "hammock."

lessons.name: Hammock: Sentence
lessons.text1: We're hanging up our new hammock in the backyard between those two tall trees.

lessons.name: Hurricane: Definition
lessons.text1: hurricane (noun): a tropical storm that includes a cyclone, high winds, rain, thunder and lightning.

lessons.name: Hurricane: History
lessons.text1: The Arawakan "hurakan" became the Spanish "huracan" before turning into the English "hurricane." Hurricanes have occured in the Caribbean for all of its recorded history, so it makes sense that the people originally from there would be the first to have a name for it!

lessons.name: Hurricane: Sentence
lessons.text1: Since the weather report is predicting a hurricane, we're making sure we have supplies like clean water and flashlights, just in case.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: hammock fishnet Caribbean supports fabric hurricane cyclone storm thunder lightning

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: We used to live on the coast, where there were a lot of hurricanes. They blew me right out of my hammock! Now we live on the savanna. In the evenings, we cook on the barbecue and see wild animals. We hung up our hammock on posts, and we don't worry about hurricanes anymore!

lessons.name: German Intro
lessons.text1: German is an official language of Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, Liechtenstein, and Luxembourg. Spoken by about 130 million people worldwide, German is famous for incredibly long and complex compound words that are theoretically endless in length.

lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some German words that have made their way into English.

lessons.name: Waltz: Definition
lessons.text1: waltz (noun or verb): a dance in which two people turn around and around in triple time. The word can also refer to the piece of music they dance to or the act of dancing this style.

lessons.name: Waltz: History
lessons.text1: "Waltz" comes from the German word "walzen," meaning "to roll," referring to the constant turning motion of the dance. Invented in Austria and Germany in the 13th century, the waltz was introduced to England in 1812, at which point the word was also introduced into the English language.

lessons.name: Waltz: Sentence
lessons.text1: They faced each other, clasped hands, and began to waltz as soon as the band started to play.

lessons.name: Hamburger: Definition
lessons.text1: hamburger (noun): a sandwich consisting of a bun with a cooked ground beef patty inside.

lessons.name: Hamburger: History
lessons.text1: For centuries, "Hamburger" meant "a person or ship from the German city of Hamburg." "Hamburg steaks" became popular in the USA around 1880 and may have been named because Hamburg was the point of departure for many German immigrants arriving at that time. However, there is no direct evidence that hamburger sandwiches are connected to the city of Hamburg.

lessons.name: Hamburger: Sentence
lessons.text1: As a vegetarian, I do not eat hamburgers, but I do eat veggieburgers and beanburgers.

lessons.name: Nickel: Definition
lessons.text1: nickel (noun): a silvery white metallic element. Also, an American five-cent coin containing 25% nickel and 75% copper.

lessons.name: Nickel: History
lessons.text1: Nickel is the name of a mischievous demon in German mythology. When 17th century copper miners tried to extract copper from nickel ore and were unable to, they called the new substance "kupfernickel," meaning "copper demon."

lessons.name: Nickel: Sentence
lessons.text1: Nickel is an element with atomic number 28 on the Periodic Table of Elements.

lessons.name: Glitch: Definition
lessons.text1: glitch (noun): a temporary malfunction that might cause delay or setback.

lessons.name: Glitch: History
lessons.text1: "Glitch" comes from the German "glitschen," meaning "to slip." In English, the word was first used in broadcasting in the mid 1900s, but was more broadly popularized by its use in the space program in the 1960s.

lessons.name: Glitch: Sentence
lessons.text1: There was a minor technological glitch, but it should be fine once we reset the system.

lessons.name: Japanese Intro
lessons.text1: Japanese is the official language of Japan and is spoken by over 125 million people worldwide. It is known for its unique writing system and its system of honorific speech.

lessons.name: Karaoke: Definition

lessons.name: Karaoke: History
lessons.text1: The word "karaoke" comes from the Japanese words "kara," meaning "empty," and "oke," short for "orchestra." Together, they describe a performance of singing to recorded music without live instruments.

lessons.name: Karaoke: Sentence

lessons.name: Origami: Definition

lessons.name: Origami: History

lessons.name: Origami: Sentence

lessons.name: Emoji: Definition

lessons.name: Emoji: History

lessons.text1: ninja (noun): a person trained in ancient Japanese martial arts and employed especially for espionage, sabotage, and infiltration.

lessons.name: Italian Intro
lessons.text1: Italian is a Romance language derived from Latin and is primarily spoken in Italy and by Italian communities worldwide. Of all the Romance languages, it is the most similar to Latin. Standard Italian is based on the Tuscan dialect of Florence. It is spoken by about 80 million people, 67 million being native speakers.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words from Italian that we use today in English!

Bravo, Barista, Fiasco, Bruschetta

lessons.name: Bravo: Definition
lessons.text1: bravo (interjection): a shout used to demonstrate approval, typically at a performance.

lessons.name: Bravo: History
lessons.text1: "Bravo" literally means "brave" in Italian. It became a popular way to applaud performers in the mid 18th century. The superlative form of bravo is bravissimo.

lessons.name: Bravo: Sentence
lessons.text1: After the opera ended, the audience leapt to their feet and shouted, "Bravo!"

lessons.name: Barista: Definition
lessons.text1: barista (noun): a person who prepares coffee as the main part of their job.

lessons.name: Barista: History
lessons.text1: "Barista" literally means "bartender" in Italian. In Italy, it refers to a worker who stands behind a bar and prepares food and drink for customers, including espresso, alcohol, and light snacks. The English use of barista began around 1992 and specifically refers to a person who makes coffee for customers.

lessons.name: Barista: Sentence
lessons.text1: The coffee shop's barista did an incredible job making my lavender honey soy milk latte with extra whipped cream!

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: bravo opera audience applaud performance barista coffee espresso shop cream

lessons.name: Fiasco: Definition
lessons.text1: fiasco (noun): something that is a huge failure, often in an embarrassing way.

lessons.name: Fiasco: History
lessons.text1: The word "fiasco" originated from the Italian phrase "fare fiasco," which literally means "make a bottle." In the mid 19th century, the term became a popular word when referring to a failed performance at the theater.

lessons.name: Fiasco: Sentence
lessons.text1: The performance was a complete fiasco because none of the actors knew their lines and the power went out halfway through the final dance number.

lessons.name: Bruschetta: Definition
lessons.text1: bruschetta: (noun): a type of bread that is roasted and drizzled in olive oil, garlic, and sometimes other toppings.

lessons.name: Bruschetta: History
lessons.text1: The word "bruschetta" comes from a Tuscan dialect called Romanesco. The verb "bruscare" means "to roast over coals" or "to toast."

lessons.name: Bruschetta: Sentence
lessons.text1: The bruschetta we made in cooking class had olive oil, garlic, and tomatoes.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: bruschetta toast garlic coals verb fiasco bottle theater failed performance

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: My sister was so nervous about her performance in the local play. "It's going to be a fiasco," she said before going on stage. However, when the curtain fell, the audience members were on their feet, clapping and cheering! One man even yelled, "Bravo!" To celebrate, I took my sister to the new Italian restaurant downtown. The barista served bruschetta with olives and garlic for a snack and cappuccinos with our dessert. Delicious!

lessons.name: Persian Intro
lessons.text1: Persian is a Middle Eastern and Central Asian language with about 112 million speakers, 62 million of which are native speakers. The language is known as Farsi in Iran, Dari in Afghanistan, and Tajik in Tajikistan.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that were adopted into English from Persian.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
pistachio pistachio pistachio
mummy mummy mummy
jasmine jasmine jasmine
magic magic magic
Pistachio, Mummy, Jasmine, Magic

lessons.name: Pistachio: Definition
lessons.text1: pistachio (noun): a small Asian tree in the cashew family whose fruit produces a hard-shelled greenish edible nut.

lessons.name: Pistachio: History
lessons.text1: The Persian word "pistah" became "pistakion" in Greek, then "pistacium" in Latin, then "pistacchio" in Italian, and "pistachio" in English.

lessons.name: Pistachio: Sentence
lessons.text1: The best ice cream flavors are always green: mint chip, matcha, pandan, and pistachio!

lessons.name: Mummy: Definition
lessons.text1: mummy (noun): a preserved and embalmed body, possibly prepared for burial in the tradition of the ancient Egyptians.

lessons.name: Mummy: History
lessons.text1: The English word "mummy" comes from the Persian "mumiya" which means "asphalt." Asphalt was used medicinally in medieval times and it was believed that the ancient Egyptians had used it for embalming. Thus, mummies were sometimes harvested for the their supposed asphalt content.

lessons.name: Mummy: Sentence
lessons.text1: We went to the Egyptian artifacts exhibition at the museum and got to see a real-life mummy!

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: pistachio Persian edible greenish mummy Egyptian asphalt embalming medicinal artifacts

lessons.name: Jasmine: Definition
lessons.text1: jasmine (noun): a climbing Asian shrub with fragrant white flowers whose oil is often used in perfume.

lessons.name: Jasmine: History
lessons.text1: Persian "yasmin" was adopted into Arabic and then into French as "jasmin," and into English as "jasmine." In Greek, "iasme" or "iasmelaion" was the name of a Persian perfume that may have used jasmine oil.

lessons.name: Jasmine: Sentence
lessons.text1: After lunch, we shared a pot of fragrant jasmine tea in the garden.

lessons.name: Magic: Definition
lessons.text1: magic (noun): a seemingly supernatural power over natural forces, sometimes using spells, charms, or incantations.

lessons.name: Magic: History
lessons.text1: In Old Persian, "magush" meant "to have power." This combined with the Greek "magos," meaning "member of the learned priestly class," to become "magike" in Greek, then "magice" meaning "sorcery" in Latin, "magique" in French, and finally the English "magic."

lessons.name: Magic: Sentence
lessons.text1: My grandpa took me to the magic shop and let me pick out a cool magic set to perform with at home.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: jasmine fragrant perfume flowers shrub magic supernatural spells charms incantation

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: Yesterday we went to a dinner show. We had a lovely meal while performers danced, sang, and told jokes. When dessert came out, a magician was performing. He turned a bouquet of jasmine into a pistachio ice cream cone! Then he said he was going to bring a mummy back to life. He brought the mummy on stage, and even though I know that magic isn't real, I decided it was time to go home.

lessons.name: Nahuatl Intro
lessons.text1: Nahuatl, also known as Aztec, refers to a group of languages of the Uto-Aztecan language family. Nahuatl was spoken by the Aztec empire in what is now central Mexico. Nahuatl influenced modern Mexican Spanish and is still spoken by around 1.5 million people today, mainly in rural areas of central Mexico. It is one of the most widely spoken indigenous languages of the Americas.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some Nahuatl words we still use today in English!

lessons.name: Tomato: Definition
lessons.text1: tomato (noun): a rounded, edible fruit, usually red and occasionally yellow, orange, or green, that is native to South America and eaten raw or cooked as a vegetable.

lessons.name: Tomato: History
lessons.text1: The word "tomato" comes from the Nahuatl word "tomatl." When the European conquistadors invaded the Americas, they wouldn't have seen a tomato before, since the fruit is indigenous to the Americas. In Portuguese, French, and Spanish, it became "tomate." Next, English adopted the loanword "tomato."

lessons.name: Tomato: Sentence
lessons.text1: Fried green tomatoes sound a little weird, but they are actually quite delicious!

lessons.name: Chili: Definition
lessons.text1: chili (noun): any pungent hot pepper used for sauces, spice powders, and relishes, chopped or dried.

lessons.name: Chili: History
lessons.text1: The Nahuatl word for "chili" is the same word we use in English - "chili!" The Spanish adopted the word to be "chile." The Anglicized version of the word comes in a variety of spellings, like chili, chile, or chille.

lessons.name: Chili: Sentence
lessons.text1: My best friend took a big bite of a hot chili pepper before I could stop her, and now her mouth is on fire!

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: tomato fruit indigenous red chili pepper spice chopped dried

lessons.name: Chocolate: Definition
lessons.text1: chocolate (noun): a food prepared from roasted and ground cacao seeds, which is typically sweetened, and can be in the form of a paste, a solid block, or a liquid.

lessons.name: Chocolate: History
lessons.text1: "Chocolate" is thought to be derived from the Nahuatl "chocolatl," referring to a bitter drink made from the cacao bean. The Aztecs drank it cold while the Spanish changed the drink to hot and called it "chocolate."

lessons.name: Chocolate: Sentence
lessons.text1: The cafe didn't serve just candies and ice cream but also hot chocolate topped with housemade whipped cream and shaved ganache.

lessons.name: Guacamole: Definition
lessons.text1: guacamole (noun): a Mexican dish consisting of pureed or mashed avocado with onion, tomatoes, chili peppers, and other seasonings.

lessons.name: Guacamole: History
lessons.text1: "Guacamole" is a Spanish word originating from Nahautl's "ahuaca-molli." "Ahuacatl" means "avocado," while "molli" means "sauce." Guacamole is an avocado sauce!

lessons.name: Guacamole: Sentence
lessons.text1: The waiter made the guacamole tableside in a large stone bowl, mashing avocado, onions, tomato, cilantro, chili pepper, and lime together.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: chocolate bitter hot cacao bean guacamole avocado sauce mashed bowl

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: Tonight was a culinary adventure with my cooking class! First, we made chiles rellenos, or stuffed poblano peppers. We used tomatoes, onions, garlic, beef, and other spices. Next, we made guacamole, complete with lime and cilantro. Finally, we ended the class by making dark hot chocolate with cayenne pepper. Delicious!

lessons.name: Dutch Intro
lessons.text1: Dutch, the official language of the Netherlands and one of the official languages of Belgium and Suriname, is spoken by roughly 30 million people worldwide. It is part of the Germanic language family and is closely related to both German and English. Dutch has a rich literary history and influenced the development of Afrikaans, a language spoken in South Africa and Namibia.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some Dutch words that we use today in English!

lessons.name: Words

waffle waffle waffle

Waffle, Frolic, Snoop, Cookie

lessons.name: Waffle: Definition
lessons.text1: waffle (noun): a crisp, leavened batter cake baked in a grid pattern, often eaten for breakfast with toppings like syrup or fruit.

lessons.name: Waffle: History
lessons.text1: The word "waffle" originates from the Dutch "wafel," which comes from the Middle Dutch "wafele." This word is related to the Old High German "waba," meaning "honeycomb," and the Old English "wefan," meaning "to weave." These meanings are reflected in the distinctive grid-like appearance of waffles.

lessons.name: Waffle: Sentence
lessons.text1: I ordered a waffle at the diner, and I added extra syrup and berries to make it even more delicious.

lessons.name: Frolic: Definition
lessons.text1: frolic (verb): to play and move about in a lively, cheerful way, often with a sense of fun and energy.

lessons.name: Frolic: History
lessons.text1: The word "frolic" comes from the Dutch "vroolijk," which is derived from the Middle Dutch "vrolijc," meaning "happy." The connection to happiness reflects the lively and playful nature of frolicking, which involves joyful and carefree movement.

lessons.name: Frolic: Sentence
lessons.text1: The kittens started to frolic in the garden, darting through the grass and pouncing on each other.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: waffle grid pattern weave grid frolic playful lively garden

lessons.name: Cookie: Definition
lessons.text1: cookie (noun): a small, sweet baked treat, typically round and made with flour, sugar, and butter.

lessons.name: Cookie: History
lessons.text1: The word "cookie" comes from the Dutch "koekje," which is the diminutive form of "koek," meaning "cake." The term "koekje" basically translates to "little cake," reflecting the small, sweet baked treat that the word represents.

lessons.name: Cookie: Sentence
lessons.text1: He baked a fresh batch of chocolate chip cookies, and the warm scent of melted chocolate filled the entire house.

lessons.name: Snoop: Definition
lessons.text1: snoop (verb): to look around or investigate in a secretive way, often trying to find out information without permission.

lessons.name: Snoop: History
lessons.text1: The word "snoop" comes from the Dutch "snoepen," meaning "to buy or eat on the sly." It is related to the Dutch word "snappen," which means "to snap," as though someone is quickly snapping up information without being noticed.

lessons.name: Snoop: Sentence
lessons.text1: She tried to snoop around her older sister's room, but she couldn't find any hidden birthday gifts no matter how hard she looked.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: cookie diminutive treat chocolate snoop investigate secretive sly birthday

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: At breakfast, Max sat at the table, cutting into his waffle and wondering where his dad had hidden the cookies he baked last night. After snooping around the kitchen with no luck, he grabbed his backpack and headed to the park to play with his friends. As they frolicked and ran around, he reached into his bag to grab his water bottle and, to his surprise, found a container of last night's cookies to share with his friends!

lessons.name: Intro Latin
lessons.text1: Latin, once the main language of the Roman Empire, is the basis for many modern languages, like Spanish, French, and Italian. Although not spoken as a native language anymore, Latin is still used in Vatican City and taught in many schools around the world. Latin is considered a dead language, but its roots are used in many English words, especially words related to science, law, medicine, and religion.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some English words that were originally from Latin.

lessons.text1:
vegetable vegetable vegetable
ambiguous ambiguous ambiguous

Vegetable, Ambiguous, Precarious, Impromptu

lessons.name: Vegetable: Definition
lessons.text1: vegetable (noun): a plant or part of a plant that is eaten as food, such as a carrot, potato, or spinach.

lessons.name: Vegetable: History
lessons.text1: The word "vegetable" comes from Latin words that mean "capable of living and growing" when combined. This connection highlights the idea of plants as living, growing things that are used as food.

lessons.name: Vegetable: Sentence
lessons.text1: Carrots are her favorite vegetable to snack on.

lessons.name: Ambiguous: Definition
lessons.text1: ambiguous (adjective): having more than one possible meaning; not clear.

lessons.name: Ambiguous: History
lessons.text1: The word "ambiguous" comes from the Latin word "ambiguus" which means "unresolved" or "untrustworthy."

lessons.name: Ambiguous: Sentence
lessons.text1: The ending of the movie was ambiguous and left viewers confused.

lessons.name: Game

lessons.name: Precarious: Definition
lessons.text1: precarious (adjective): not safe or secure; likely to fall or get worse.

lessons.name: Precarious: History
lessons.text1: The word "precarious" comes from the Latin word "precarius," which originally meant "obtained by entreaty or prayer." Over time, "precarius" came to mean "doubtful" or "uncertain."

lessons.name: Precarious: Sentence
lessons.text1: The ladder looked precarious, so he was careful climbing it.

lessons.name: Impromptu: Definition
lessons.text1: impromptu (adjective): done without planning or preparation.

lessons.name: Impromptu: History
lessons.text1: The word "impromptu" comes from the Latin term "in promptu," which means "in readiness" or "ready to be brought forward."

lessons.name: Impromptu: Sentence
lessons.text1: We decided to have an impromptu pizza party after school.

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: During her impromptu visit to the local farmer's market, Anna decided to buy fresh vegetables for dinner. As she was shopping, she noticed a few zucchinis were balanced in a precarious position on the edge of the stall. She carefully moved them to a safer spot and continued browsing. The zucchini bread recipe she received from the vendor was a bit ambiguous, but she was excited to experiment in the kitchen.

lessons.name: Greek Intro
lessons.text1: Greek is the official language of Greece and Cyprus, and it is also recognized as a minority language in several countries, including Albania, Italy, and Turkey. It holds historical significance as one of the world's oldest written languages. Modern Greek is spoken by around 13 million people.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that came to English from Greek.

lessons.name: Dinosaur: Definition
lessons.text1: dinosaur (noun): any of a group (Dinosauria) of extinct and often very large reptiles which flourished during the Mesozoic era.

lessons.name: Dinosaur: History
lessons.text1: The word "dinosaur" comes from two Greek words meaning "lizard" and "inspiring dread or awe." This name reflects the enormous size and fearsome appearance of these ancient creatures.

lessons.name: Dinosaur: Sentence
lessons.text1: The Tyrannosaurus rex is one of the most well-known species of dinosaur.

lessons.name: Planet: Definition
lessons.text1: planet (noun): a large, round object in space that orbits a star, such as the Sun.

lessons.name: Planet: History
lessons.text1: The word "planet" comes from a Greek word which means "wanderer." This term was used by ancient astronomers to describe celestial bodies that appeared to wander across the sky.

lessons.name: Planet: Sentence
lessons.text1: Earth is the third planet from the Sun in our solar system, and it is known for its diverse ecosystems.

lessons.name: Galaxy: Definition
lessons.text1: galaxy (noun): any of the very large groups of stars and associated matter that are found throughout the universe.

lessons.name: Galaxy: History
lessons.text1: The word "galaxy" originates from a Greek word meaning "milky." It refers to the Milky Way, the galaxy that contains our solar system, and derives from the Greek myth of the milk of the goddess Hera.

lessons.name: Galaxy: Sentence
lessons.text1: The Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our solar system, and it is home to billions of stars and planets.

lessons.name: Democracy: Definition
lessons.text1: democracy (noun): a system of government where the people have the power to make decisions through voting, either directly or by electing representatives.

lessons.name: Democracy: History
lessons.text1: The word "democracy" comes from two Greek words meaning "people" and "power or rule." It was used in ancient Greece to describe a system of government where the power lies with the people.

lessons.name: Democracy: Sentence
lessons.text1: In a democracy, citizens actively participate in the decision-making process by voting and engaging in public debates.

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: I started reading a new sci-fi novel about a distant galaxy. At the beginning of the story, scientists find a world with dinosaur fossils like the ones on Earth. This discovery leads to a lot of scientific debate, showcasing the spirit of democracy as people from different backgrounds and disciplines share their views. But just when they think they've discussed all possible theories, the hero detects a mysterious signal coming from the planet's core!

lessons.name: Sanskrit Intro
lessons.text1: Sanskrit is an ancient language of India. Today, only about 14,000 people speak it as their primary language, though it is commonly used in Hindu religious services. Sanskrit is also the root of several modern Indian languages, including Hindi, which has about 545 million speakers.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: The English language has adopted a variety of words from Sanskrit, sometimes by way of Hindi. Let's practice typing a few of them.

lessons.name: Avatar: Definition
lessons.text1: avatar (noun): an electronic image that represents and might be controlled by the computer user, for example in a video game.

lessons.name: Avatar: History
lessons.text1: "Avatar" comes from the Sanskrit "avatarana," meaning "descent (of a deity to Earth in human form)." It came to mean "embodiment" more widely, including of ideas and philosophies, before taking on the electronic sense in the early 1990s.

lessons.name: Avatar: Sentence
lessons.text1: Before starting the game, you can create your avatar to look like yourself or someone completely different.

lessons.name: Yoga: Definition
lessons.text1: yoga (noun): a practice of physical, mental, and breathing exercises intended to give the practitioner control over mind and body.

lessons.name: Yoga: History
lessons.text1: The word "yoga" came from Sanskrit into Hindi and then into English. It literally translates to "union" or "joining." Originally this referred to uniting the self with a higher spiritual entity, and later to uniting one's own mind, body, and spirit.

lessons.name: Yoga: Sentence
lessons.text1: They changed into loose, comfortable clothing for the evening yoga class.

lessons.name: Cheetah: Definition
lessons.text1: cheetah (noun): a swift African and Asian cat the size of a small leopard, with tan and white fur covered in small black spots.

lessons.name: Cheetah: History
lessons.text1: In Sanskrit, "citraka" means "bright" or "variegated," referring to the markings on a cheetah's body. The word moved into Hindi and Urdu as "chita," meaning "leopard," before coming into English.

lessons.name: Cheetah: Sentence
lessons.text1: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching a running speed of up to 60 mph (100 kph).

lessons.name: Karma: Definition
lessons.text1: karma (noun): the effects of a person's actions on their destiny where good deeds yield good fortune and bad deeds yield bad fortune.

lessons.name: Karma: History
lessons.text1: "Karma" is a Sanskrit word literally meaning "action," or "fate," though it came to mean "the sum of a person's actions in their lifetime." This is rooted in the Hindu and Buddhist concept of reincarnation, though in English the word's usage is not necessarily predicated on reincarnation.

lessons.name: Karma: Sentence
lessons.text1: They hoped that doing volunteer work and donating money to good causes would contribute to their good karma.

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: I downloaded a new app for my phone that has prerecorded yoga classes on it. It has a bunch of cute animal avatars to choose from. I chose a cheetah. Perhaps I can add to my good karma by calming my mind with yoga and acting more compassionately towards others.

lessons.name: Russian Intro
lessons.text1: There are about 270 million Russian speakers worldwide. Russian is a Slavic language and the official language of Russia, but it is also widely used in countries across Central Asia and Eastern Europe that were formerly part of the Soviet Union.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Russian has adopted many words from other European languages, but English has also adopted words from Russian. Let's practice typing a few of them.

lessons.name: Babushka: Definition
lessons.text1: babushka (noun): a triangular folded scarf or kerchief worn over the head. Also, an elderly Russian woman.

lessons.name: Babushka: History
lessons.text1: "Babushka" means grandmother in Russian. In Russian the emphasis is on the first syllable, while in English it's on the second, making the pronunciations slightly different.

lessons.name: Babushka: Sentence
lessons.text1: She tied the babushka over her head before going out so her hair wouldn't get too tangled in the windy weather.

lessons.name: Beluga: Definition
lessons.text1: beluga (noun): a small white whale with teeth that is found mostly in Arctic waters.

lessons.name: Beluga: History
lessons.text1: "Beluga" translates literally from Russian as "great white." It originally referred to large white sturgeon fish found in the Black and Caspian Seas. In the early 1800s, it came to be more used for small white whales in the northern seas.

lessons.name: Beluga: Sentence
lessons.text1: Beluga calves are usually born gray, but they lose their color as they grow and are usually white by the time they are about 7-9 years old.

lessons.name: Samovar: Definition
lessons.text1: samovar (noun): an urn with a spigot and heating mechanism used to boil and pour water for tea.

lessons.name: Samovar: History
lessons.text1: In Russian, "samo" means "self" and "varit" means "to boil," so "samovar" can be literally translated as "self-boiler."

lessons.name: Samovar: Sentence
lessons.text1: He came in from the cold and immediately poured himself a cup of tea from the copper samovar on the counter.

lessons.name: Blini: Definition
lessons.text1: blini (noun): round pancakes traditionally made with yeast and buckwheat flour, though they are now made with any kind of flour, with or without yeast. They are usually filled or topped with sour cream, caviar, or fruit preserves.

lessons.name: Blini: History
lessons.text1: Blini were made by pre-Christian Slavic peoples at the end of winter as a symbol of the sun. They were primarily made for a week-long celebration known as Butter Week or Pancake Week, where people believed that making and eating many delicious blini would bring good fortune for the coming spring and summer.

lessons.name: Blini: Sentence
lessons.text1: Blini have become a popular dish worldwide, not just for celebrations but as a sweet or savory breakfast.

lessons.name: Hebrew Intro
lessons.text1: Hebrew was widely spoken in Jewish communities up until the second century BCE. It was then used in religious texts but rarely spoken for about 2,000 years, until it was revived as a spoken language in the late 1800s. Today, there are about 15 million Hebrew-speakers worldwide, and Hebrew is the official language of Israel.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: When Hebrew was first revived as an everyday spoken language, it needed new words for modern concepts. Some words were adopted from other languages and some were made up. English has also adopted words that were originally Hebrew. Let's practice typing some of them.

lessons.text1:

klezmer klezmer klezmer
matzoh matzoh matzoh

Jubilee, Klezmer, Matzoh, Maven

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Hebrew revived Israel everyday concepts adopted jubilee klezmer matzoh maven

lessons.name: Jubilee: Definition
lessons.text1: jubilee (noun): the celebration of an important event that happened many years ago.

lessons.name: Jubilee: History
lessons.text1: "Jubilee" originated with the Hebrew word "yobhel," which means "ram." A musical instrument made from a ram's horn is blown like a trumpet to celebrate certain important Jewish holidays.

lessons.name: Jubilee: Sentence
lessons.text1: There will be a parade and a boat race this summer to mark the Queen's diamond jubilee.

lessons.name: Klezmer: Definition
lessons.text1: klezmer (noun): a musical genre deriving from and building on traditional eastern European Jewish music.

lessons.name: Klezmer: History
lessons.text1: The Hebrew roots "klei," vessel, and "zemer," song, traditionally referred to a male musician as "klezmer." Around the year 1980, the term became more associated with the type of music than the person playing it.

lessons.name: Klezmer: Sentence
lessons.text1: The concert hall hosted a classical orchestra last week and will have a klezmer band this week.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: jubilee celebration musical instrument parade Hebrew klezmer genre traditional musician

lessons.name: Matzoh: Definition
lessons.text1: matzoh (noun): unleavened bread traditionally eaten during the Jewish holiday of Passover.

lessons.name: Matzoh: History
lessons.text1: "Matzoh" originated from the Hebrew stem "matzatz," which literally translates to "drained out," since matzoh is unleavened and dry.

lessons.name: Matzoh: Sentence
lessons.text1: Supermarkets around the world sell all kinds of delicious matzoh, including salted, whole wheat, onion-flavored, cinnamon-dusted, and even chocolate-covered.

lessons.name: Maven: Definition
lessons.text1: maven (noun): a person who is very knowledgable or an expert on a certain subject.

lessons.name: Maven: History
lessons.text1: "Maven" originally comes from the Hebrew word "mebhin," which translates to "one who understands."

lessons.name: Maven: Sentence
lessons.text1: After finishing a degree in design and working in the garment industry for a decade, he has become quite the fashion maven.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: matzoh unleavened holiday supermarket cinnamon maven knowledgable expert understands

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: The college we went to is celebrating its 100-year jubilee. There will be bands playing all kinds of music, including rock, jazz, klezmer, classical, and blues. Let's go listen on the lawn. I'll bring matzoh, olives, fruit, and cheese to snack on. There will also be a speech by an alumnus who has become a business maven.

lessons.name: Mandarin Intro
lessons.text1: Mandarin is the official language of China. It is a tonal language, meaning that the same syllable has different meanings depending on the tone being used. Mandarin has four tones. With roughly 900 million speakers worldwide, it's the most commonly spoken language in the world.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that came to English from Mandarin.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
feng shui feng shui feng shui
tofu tofu tofu
yin yang yin yang yin yang
qi qi qi
Feng shui, Tofu, Yin yang, Qi

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Mandarin China tonal official different meanings tofu yin yang qi

lessons.name: Feng shui: Definition
lessons.text1: feng shui (noun): an ancient Chinese practice of arranging spaces to be in harmony with the natural world and bring prosperity.

lessons.name: Feng shui: History
lessons.text1: "Feng shui" means "wind and water." It is the art of arranging a physical environment, such as a room or building, to be in harmony with natural forces. This is thought to bring peace and prosperity.

lessons.name: Feng shui: Sentence
lessons.text1: To improve the feng shui of the bedroom, I moved the bed to face the door and placed nightstands on either side.

lessons.name: Tofu: Definition
lessons.text1: tofu (noun): a soft, white food made from soybeans that is high in protein.

lessons.name: Tofu: History
lessons.text1: "Tofu" can be traced back to the Mandarin word "doufu," meaning "fermented beans." Made from curdled soybean milk, tofu is a staple in many Asian cuisines. It became popular in English-speaking countries in the later 20th century.

lessons.name: Tofu: Sentence
lessons.text1: The cookbook included a vegetarian version of the recipe that called for tofu instead of chicken.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: harmony Mandarin wind water natural prosperity tofu soybeans protein healthy

lessons.name: Yin yang: Definition
lessons.text1: yin and yang (noun): the idea of opposite but complementary forces that create a balance; the duality of all things.

lessons.name: Yin yang: History
lessons.text1: Yin and yang is the concept that there are two opposite forces that create a balance in nature. It comes from "yin," which is associated with feminine energy and the moon, and "yang," which is associated with masculine energy and the sun. It is believed that everything possesses both yin and yang.

lessons.name: Yin yang: Sentence
lessons.text1: Our teacher explained that the yin and yang symbol is a circle that is half black and half white, representing how neither force can exist without the other.

lessons.name: Qi: Definition
lessons.text1: qi (noun): the life force that flows through and regulates the body.

lessons.name: Qi: History
lessons.text1: In traditional Chinese medicine, qi is the vital force that circulates through the body as well as the whole universe. Regulating one's qi, such as through exercise, martial arts, or acupuncture, is considered essential for good health.

lessons.name: Qi: Sentence
lessons.text1: The doctor suggested drinking herbal tea and practicing tai chi every day in order to improve the flow of our qi.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: yin yang opposite balance qi life force traditional medicine nature regulate

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: After a tasty lunch of fried tofu and veggies, I rearranged the furniture to improve the feng shui in my home. Then I walked to the bookstore, where I found a book with a yin and yang symbol on the cover. It gave suggestions to improve my qi flow and live a healthier lifestyle.

lessons.name: Quechua Intro
lessons.text1: Quechua is famous for being the language of the Incas, originating in the Andes region of South America. Today there are about 45 dialects of Quechua and about 10 million speakers.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing a few words that were adopted into English from Quechua.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
llama llama llama
quinoa quinoa quinoa
puma puma puma
jerky jerky jerky
Llama, Quinoa, Puma, Jerky

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Quechua Inca Andes South America dialects llama quinoa puma jerky

lessons.name: Llama: Definition
lessons.text1: llama (noun): a large South American mammal with a long neck that is often kept for its wool or to carry heavy loads.

lessons.name: Llama: History
lessons.text1: Llamas are a relative of camels and alpacas. They are native to South America. The word "llama" came directly from Quechua into Spanish and then English.

lessons.name: Llama: Sentence
lessons.text1: We got to pet a gentle, furry llama at the petting zoo yesterday.

lessons.name: Quinoa: Definition
lessons.text1: quinoa (noun): the seeds of a South American plant that are cooked and eaten as a nutritious food.

lessons.name: Quinoa: History
lessons.text1: The original spelling of "kinua" was turned into "quinoa" when it was adopted into Spanish to better align with Spanish phonetic rules. It remained as "quinoa" when the word subsequently came into English.

lessons.name: Quinoa: Sentence
lessons.text1: He cooked a big pot of quinoa to have along with the vegetables and meat he had prepared for lunch.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: llama mammal Quechua wool zoo quinoa nutritious phonetic vegetables prepared

lessons.name: Puma: Definition
lessons.text1: puma (noun): a large brown wildcat that lives across the whole of North and South America.

lessons.name: Puma: History
lessons.text1: "Puma" is a Quechua word that was adopted into Spanish and then English. In English, there are regional variations in what people call pumas, including mountain lions, cougars, or panthers.

lessons.name: Puma: Sentence
lessons.text1: Every now and then a puma comes down the mountain and shows up in our backyard.

lessons.name: Jerky: Definition
lessons.text1: jerky (noun): meat, cut into strips and dried.

lessons.name: Jerky: History
lessons.text1: In Quechua, "ch'arki" literally translates to "dried flesh." This was adopted into American Spanish as "charqui," meaning "dried, salted meat," and from there into American English as "jerky."

lessons.name: Jerky: Sentence
lessons.text1: We packed our backpacks with trail mix, beef jerky, and plenty of water for the long hike.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: puma wildcat regional panther cougar jerky strips salted dried

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: Llamas love to eat quinoa. In the wild they help more quinoa plants grow by spreading the seeds. Pumas, on the other hand, are obligate carnivores, like all felines. They would probably enjoy a piece of beef jerky a lot more than a bowl of quinoa.

lessons.name: Bantu Languages Intro
lessons.text1: The Bantu language family consists of about 600 different languages in West Africa. It is estimated that 350 million people speak Bantu languages. One of the most widely spoken Bantu languages is Swahili, with approximately 16 million native speakers.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing words from the Bantu language family that we use in English today.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
banjo banjo banjo
gumbo gumbo gumbo
marimba marimba marimba

Banjo, Gumbo, Marimba, Macaque

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Bantu family West Africa Swahili approximately banjo gumbo marimba macaque

lessons.name: Banjo: Definition
lessons.text1: banjo (noun): a stringed musical instrument with a drum-like body that is either plucked or strummed.

lessons.name: Banjo: History
lessons.text1: The word "banjo" is likely an alteration of the Kimbundu (a Bantu language) word "mbanza," which is the name for a stringed instrument somewhat similar to the modern banjo.

lessons.name: Banjo: Sentence
lessons.text1: The highlight of the bluegrass jam was the energetic banjo solo.

lessons.name: Gumbo: Definition
lessons.text1: gumbo (noun): an aromatic Creole stew thickened with okra that typically contains meat or seafood as well as vegetables.

lessons.name: Gumbo: History
lessons.text1: The word "gumbo" developed out of Louisiana French, probably originating from "ngombo," meaning "okra" in Central Bantu dialects. Gumbo is typically thickened with okra.

lessons.name: Gumbo: Sentence
lessons.text1: Louisiana's state cuisine is gumbo, so of course we had to try some while on vacation in New Orleans.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: banjo instrument drum plucked strummed gumbo okra seafood stew Louisiana

lessons.name: Marimba: Definition
lessons.text1: marimba (noun): an instrument consisting of wooden bars with resonators beneath for amplification, originating in southern Africa but popularized in Central America.

lessons.name: Marimba: History
lessons.text1: "Marimba" comes from the Bantu languages of Kimbundu and Swahili via Portuguese in the early 18th century.

lessons.name: Marimba: Sentence
lessons.text1: The warm, resonant tones of the marimba filled the room, and soon, everyone was clapping along.

lessons.name: Macaque: Definition
lessons.text1: macaque (noun): any genus of Old World monkeys, chiefly dwelling in Asia, which typically have a medium build, a long face, and cheek pouches.

lessons.name: Macaque: History
lessons.text1: Portuguese adopted "macaco," meaning "monkey," from Bantu, which then became "macaque" in French. In 1840, it was introduced as a genus name.

lessons.name: Macaque: Sentence
lessons.text1: Long-tailed macaques discovered their own method of cleaning sand off of fruit by rinsing the fruit in the river.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: marimba wooden amplification Africa Kimbundu Swahili macaque monkey French genus

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: We had a full day planned. First, we went to the zoo. My favorite part was watching the long-tailed macaques jump from tree to tree. Next, we went to a concert with many unique instruments, including a five-string banjo and a wooden marimba. Finally, we finished our day with an authentic bowl of gumbo, full of okra, seafood, spices, and vegetables.

lessons.name: Malay Intro
lessons.text1: Malay, also known as Bahasa Melayu, has about 220 million speakers across several dialects, including Bahasa Indonesia and Bahasa Malaysia. Malay is an official language of Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Brunei but also has many speakers in other Southeast Asian countries, such as Thailand and East Timor.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that came from Malay into English.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
gecko gecko gecko
durian durian durian
orangutan orangutan orangutan
sarong sarong sarong
Gecko, Durian, Orangutan, Sarong

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Malay Bahasa Malaysia Indonesia Singapore Brunei gecko durian orangutan sarong

lessons.name: Gecko: Definition
lessons.text1: gecko (noun): a small lizard with wide feet that lives in warm habitats.

lessons.name: Gecko: History
lessons.text1: The Malay word "gekoq" may have come from an imitation of the sound the lizard makes. The word came into English in the early 1700s as "chacco" and then evolved into "jackoa" and finally "gecko."

lessons.name: Gecko: Sentence
lessons.text1: The gecko crawled up the wall, behind the curtain, and onto the ceiling.

lessons.name: Durian: Definition
lessons.text1: durian (noun): a large, spiky, oval fruit with a sweet taste and pungent odor.

lessons.name: Durian: History
lessons.text1: The Malay word "duri" means thorn or prickle, so "durian" is a fitting name for the prickly fruit. The word was adopted into English in the 1580s.

lessons.name: Durian: Sentence
lessons.text1: It is forbidden to eat durian in some hotels because the strong aroma might be bothersome to other guests.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Malaysia Indonesia Malay gecko lizard durian spiky pungent prickly aroma

lessons.name: Orangutan: Definition
lessons.text1: orangutan (noun): a large ape with long arms and reddish-brown hair that lives in the forests of some Indonesian islands.

lessons.name: Orangutan: History
lessons.text1: The Malay word "orang" means "man," and "utan" or "hutan" means "forest" or "wilderness." Put together, "orangutan" literally translates to "man of the wild forest."

lessons.name: Orangutan: Sentence
lessons.text1: The gentle orangutan reached out her leathery, human-like hand to pick the lychee from the tree branch.

lessons.name: Sarong: Definition
lessons.text1: sarong (noun): a long piece of cloth worn wrapped around the body as a loose garment. It is worn by men and women primarily in the South Pacific and Malay Archipelago.

lessons.name: Sarong: History
lessons.text1: In Malay, "sarung" means "sheath" or "covering." The sarong is the national garment of Malaysia, but similar garments are worn in many parts of Asia, Africa, and Oceania.

lessons.name: Sarong: Sentence
lessons.text1: They used wax and colorful dyes to create beautiful patterns on the sarong fabric.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: orangutan wilderness forest islands gentle sarong garment sheath covering archipelago

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: I tucked in the loose end of my sarong and walked along the forest path. A gecko skittered up a durian tree and stood lightly on a branch next to the spiky fruit. A few minutes later, I spotted an orangutan high up in another tree, lazily gnawing on a mango.

lessons.name: Australian Aboriginal Languages Intro
lessons.text1: Australian Aboriginal languages are the languages spoken by the Indigenous people of Australia. There are over 250 Indigenous Australian languages, though only about 20 are actively spoken today.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Let's practice typing some words that came to English from different Australian Aboriginal languages.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
boomerang boomerang boomerang
kangaroo kangaroo kangaroo
koala koala koala
kookaburra kookaburra kookaburra
Boomerang, Kangaroo, Koala, Kookaburra

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Australian Aboriginal indigenous Australia actively spoken boomerang kangaroo koala kookaburra

lessons.name: Boomerang: Definition
lessons.text1: boomerang (noun): a bent piece of wood that is curved on one side and flat on the other and that, when thrown, will return to the thrower.

lessons.name: Boomerang: History
lessons.text1: The word "boomerang" comes from the Dharug language. While it often refers to the iconic curved throwing stick, it can also be used as a verb describing something, like a plan, that backfires on the person who produced it.

lessons.name: Boomerang: Sentence
lessons.text1: As a kid, I would often go to the park to throw a boomerang, though it took a lot of practice before I could catch it.

lessons.name: Kangaroo: Definition
lessons.text1: kangaroo (noun): a large, leaping marsupial with powerful hind legs and a long tail used for balance.

lessons.name: Kangaroo: History
lessons.text1: "Kangaroo" comes from the Guugu Yimidhirr language. The original word, "gangurru," referred specifically to the eastern gray kangaroo. Kangaroos are recognized as a national symbol of Australia, appearing on stamps, currency, and the Australian coat of arms.

lessons.name: Kangaroo: Sentence
lessons.text1: The startled kangaroo turned and leapt out of the yard, its powerful jump carrying it over the hedge with ease.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Australia Aboriginal kangaroo leap powerful boomerang throw stick return

lessons.name: Koala: Definition
lessons.text1: koala (noun): a gray, furry, tree-dwelling marsupial that mainly eats eucalyptus leaves.

lessons.name: Koala: History
lessons.text1: The word "koala" comes from the Dharug word "gula," which means "no drink." This has to do with the fact that koalas rarely need to drink water. Their diet consists primarily of fresh eucalyptus leaves, which give them most of the moisture they need.

lessons.name: Koala: Sentence
lessons.text1: Zoo visitors gathered around to see the sleepy koala nestled in the branches of the eucalyptus tree.

lessons.name: Kookaburra: Definition
lessons.text1: kookaburra (noun): a brown and beige bird from the kingfisher family with a loud, distinctive call that sounds like laughter.

lessons.name: Kookaburra: History
lessons.text1: "Kookaburra" comes from the Wiradjuri word "gugubarra," which is meant to imitate the sound of the bird's territorial call. At dawn and dusk, a family of kookaburras will release a call that sounds like loud, harsh laughter.

lessons.name: Kookaburra: Sentence
lessons.text1: They were woken at the campsite early in the morning by the distinctive laughter of a kookaburra.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: eucalyptus leaves water koala marsupial laughter call kookaburra bird branches

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: Before our tour of the outback began, our guide demonstrated how to use a boomerang. Then we drove to a grove of eucalyptus trees and saw koalas eating leaves off of the branches. On our way to the next site, we saw a group of kangaroos leaping along the side of the road. When we made camp that night, the startling laughter of a kookaburra family in the trees made us all laugh along.

lessons.name: Hokkien Intro
lessons.text1: Hokkien is a language originating from the Fujian province of China. It is widely spoken across southeast Asia, including in Malaysia, Taiwan, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Singapore. More than 40 million people speak Hokkien worldwide.

lessons.name: Let's Practice
lessons.text1: Many words have been adopted to the English language from Hokkien. Let's practice typing some of them.

lessons.name: Words
lessons.text1:
ginseng ginseng ginseng
ketchup ketchup ketchup
oolong oolong oolong
tea tea tea
Ginseng, Ketchup, Oolong, Tea

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: Hokkien Fujian China Taiwan Philippines Singapore ginseng ketchup oolong tea

lessons.name: Ginseng: Definition
lessons.text1: ginseng (noun): a plant with a fleshy root that has medicinal properties and is used for herbal remedies.

lessons.name: Ginseng: History
lessons.text1: The word "ginseng" comes from the Hokkien word "jin-sim" and usually refers to the root of the ginseng plant. It is used as a natural remedy to reduce stress, increase energy, and improve overall health.

lessons.name: Ginseng: Sentence
lessons.text1: The herbalist recommended that I take ginseng supplements to improve my focus.

lessons.name: Ketchup: Definition
lessons.text1: ketchup (noun): a sweet and sour condiment made from pureed tomatoes.

lessons.name: Ketchup: History
lessons.text1: The word "ketchup" comes from the Hokkien word "ke-tsiap," which refers to a fermented fish sauce first encountered by English-speakers in the late 17th century. The tomato-based sauce we know today wasn't invented until the 1800s.

lessons.name: Ketchup: Sentence
lessons.text1: She reached for the ketchup bottle and squeezed some onto the plate beside her fries.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: ginseng herbal root health ketchup tomato sauce condiment

lessons.name: Oolong: Definition
lessons.text1: oolong (noun): a dark-colored Chinese tea that is made from partially oxidized leaves.

lessons.name: Oolong: History
lessons.text1: "Oolong" came to English from the Hokkien word "o-liong," which means "black dragon." This tea is unique because it is made from the same leaves as black and green tea but falls in between the two in terms of flavor and caffeine content.

lessons.name: Oolong: Sentence
lessons.text1: We sipped fragrant oolong tea on the porch as we enjoyed the mountain view.

lessons.name: Tea: Definition
lessons.text1: tea (noun): a fragrant beverage made by soaking tea leaves in boiling water.

lessons.name: Tea: History
lessons.text1: The word "tea" is derived from the Hokkien word "te." Tea originated in China and was traded around the world. It was primarily shipped to England from the part of China that spoke Hokkien, which is why English-speakers adopted the Hokkien word for tea.

lessons.name: Tea: Sentence
lessons.text1: He poured hot water over the tea leaves, watching as they unfurled at the bottom of the teapot.

lessons.name: Game
lessons.text1: oolong dragon flavor black green oxidized tea leaves China caffeine fragrant trade

lessons.name: Paragraph
lessons.text1: Jars of tea leaves lined the walls of the shop. I bought some oolong, which was dark green and rolled into balls. My brother bought some ginseng, which the shopkeeper suggested to increase his energy. Our sister wasn't interested in herbs or tea. She was in the store next door, buying a bottle of ketchup instead!

lessons.name: Well Done!
lessons.text1:
Congratulations on finishing the Loanwords Typing course!
You've practiced typing definitions, etymologies, and paragraphs with words that came into English from other languages. You used all of the letters on the keyboard as well as numbers and symbols.
Way to go!
